translations.literal: Southern Suburbs
translations.idiomatic: Southern Suburban Sacrifice

sentences.zh: =南郊樂舞歌辭，二漢同用，見《前漢志》，五郊互奏之。

translations.literal: Southern suburban music-and-dance lyrics: both Han dynasties used them alike, as in the Former Han Treatise; the five suburban rites performed them in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Lyrics for southern suburban music and dance: Eastern and Western Han used the same set, recorded in the Former Han Treatise, with the five suburban rites taking turns to perform them.

sentences.zh: 魏歌舞不見，疑是用漢辭也。

translations.literal: Wei songs and dances are not attested; it is suspected they used Han lyrics.
translations.idiomatic: Wei-period songs and dances are not recorded; they probably kept the Han texts.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝，郊祀明堂，詔禮遵用周室肇稱殷祀之義，權用魏儀。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Jin, for suburban sacrifice and the Bright Hall, ordered ritual to follow the Zhou meaning of founding the state and naming the Yin sacrifice, provisionally using Wei rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Jin sacrificed at the suburbs and in the Bright Hall, he ordered ritual to follow the Zhou idea of founding the state and styling the offering an Yin sacrifice, and for the time being to use Wei practice.

sentences.zh: 後使傅玄造《祠天地五郊夕牲歌》詩一篇，《迎神歌》一篇。

translations.literal: Later he had Fu Xuan compose one poem, "Evening Victim Song for the Temples to Heaven and Earth and the Five Suburbs," and one "Song for Welcoming the Spirits."
translations.idiomatic: He later had Fu Xuan write one "Evening Victim Song for Heaven, Earth, and the Five Suburbs" and one "Song for Welcoming the Spirits."

sentences.zh: 宋文帝使顏延之造《郊天夕牲》、《迎送神》、《饗神歌》詩三篇，是則宋初又仍晉也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Song had Yan Yanzhi compose three poems—"Heaven-Suburb Evening Victims," "Welcoming and Sending the Spirits," and "Feasting the Spirits"—so early Song again followed Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Song had Yan Yanzhi compose three pieces—"Heaven-Suburb Evening Victims," "Welcoming and Sending the Spirits," and "Feasting the Spirits"—and early Song thus continued Jin practice.

sentences.zh: ，有司奏，郊廟雅樂歌辭舊使學士博士撰，搜簡採用，請敕外，凡肄學者普令制立。

translations.literal: , the relevant offices memorialized: for suburban and temple court-music lyrics, academicians and erudites had formerly been charged to draft them, to be searched, culled, and adopted; they asked that an edict go to the outer offices that all enrolled students be generally ordered to compose and fix them.
translations.idiomatic: , the relevant offices reported: suburban and temple court-music texts had long been drafted by academicians and erudites, then sifted and adopted; they asked for an imperial order to the outer offices requiring every student in training to compose and establish them.

sentences.zh: 參議：太廟登歌宜用司徒褚淵，餘悉用黃門郎謝超宗辭。

translations.literal: After deliberation: for the Grand Temple ascent hymn, Steward Chu Yuan's wording should be used; for the rest, entirely the wording of Yellow Gate Gentleman Xie Chao-zong.
translations.idiomatic: On review: the Grand Temple ascent hymn should use Steward Chu Yuan; everything else should use Yellow Gate Gentleman Xie Chao-zong.

sentences.zh: 超宗所撰，多刪顏延之、謝莊辭以爲新曲，備改樂名。

translations.literal: What Chao-zong composed mostly cut Yan Yanzhi's and Xie Zhuang's wording to make new tunes, thoroughly changing music titles.
translations.idiomatic: Chao-zong's work largely trimmed Yan Yanzhi and Xie Zhuang to fashion new pieces and renamed the music throughout.

sentences.zh: ，太子步兵校尉伏曼容上表，宜集英儒，刪纂雅樂。

translations.literal: , Vice Commandant of Infantry for the Heir Apparent Fu Manrong submitted a memorial: worthy scholars should be assembled to edit and compile court music.
translations.idiomatic: , Heir Apparent Vice Commandant of Infantry Fu Manrong memorialized that eminent scholars should be gathered to revise and compile court ritual music.

translations.literal: An edict assigned the matter to the outer offices for detailed review; in the end it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The court referred it to the outer offices for review, but nothing came of it.

translations.literal: When the multitude of ministers entered and exited, they performed "Music of Solemn Awe":
translations.idiomatic: As ministers entered and left, they played "Music of Solemn Awe":

translations.literal: : Reverently receiving the precious mandate, solemnly revering the imperial line.
translations.idiomatic: : Reverently taking up the sacred charge, in grave respect for the imperial succession.

translations.literal: Suddenly receiving the broad grant, ascending the center and expanding the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Receiving the far-reaching gift, rising to the center and broadening the domain.

translations.literal: Spanning the earth, styled emperor; exhausting heaven, ruling as lord.
translations.idiomatic: Across the land he is called emperor; under all heaven he stands as sovereign.

translations.literal: From the moon's domains come treasures; from the sun's verge they offer soil.
translations.idiomatic: From the western marches come tribute; from the eastern edge they present earth.

translations.literal: The inaugural origin is set right; ritual is exchanged and music raised.
translations.idiomatic: The founding year is set aright; rites are exchanged and music is lifted up.

translations.literal: The six canons link their affairs; the nine officers array their order.
translations.idiomatic: The six statutes join in their tasks; the nine ranks stand in their sequence.

translations.literal: Below this, four lines were removed.
translations.idiomatic: Four lines below were cut.

translations.literal: All are Yan's wording.
translations.idiomatic: All from Yan [Yanzhi].

translations.literal: When victims were brought in and out, they performed "Music for Leading the Victims":
translations.idiomatic: When the victims entered and left, they played "Music for Leading the Victims":

translations.literal: : August indeed is reverence; reverently serving the upper spirits.
translations.idiomatic: : How august is reverence; in respect one serves the spirits above.

translations.literal: The bright teaching, national sacrifice, solemn and clear.
translations.idiomatic: The bright teaching of state sacrifice, solemn and luminous.

translations.literal: There are victims in the pen; there is purity on the stand.
translations.idiomatic: Victims wait in the enclosure; offerings lie clean on the trays.

translations.literal: To present the king's inmost heart, to answer the spirits' blessing.
translations.idiomatic: To offer the king's true heart, to repay the spirits' grace.

translations.literal: The four lines above are Yan's wording.
translations.idiomatic: The four lines above are Yan's.

translations.literal: Ascending to match in the capital, descending virtue among the people.
translations.idiomatic: He ascends to join the sacrifice in the capital; his virtue descends to the people.

translations.literal: The rushing essence awaits the night; the lofty brazier waits for dawn.
translations.idiomatic: The swift spirit watches for night; the high flame awaits the morning.

sentences.zh: 薦豆呈毛血，奏《嘉薦之樂》：

translations.literal: Presenting beans and displaying hair and blood, they performed "Music of Fine Offering":
translations.idiomatic: When beans were offered and hair and blood shown, they played "Music of Fine Offering":

translations.literal: : I revere, I offer; only in the first month of spring.
translations.idiomatic: : With reverence I worship, with reverence I feast—only in the first month of spring.

translations.literal: With filial piety, with reverence, establishing my teeming people.
translations.idiomatic: In filial piety and in respect, he establishes his countless people.

translations.literal: The blue altar shrouded in mist; the green canopy poised and still.
translations.idiomatic: The azure altar lies in haze; the green awning hangs straight and still.

translations.literal: Fine stands offered again; layered mats raised a second time.
translations.idiomatic: Fine trays are offered again; layered mats are set once more.

translations.literal: Setting frames and setting bell-stands, displaying dignity in the jade court.
translations.idiomatic: Frames and bell-stands are set out; ceremony unfolds in the jade hall.

translations.literal: Beginning the suburban match-sacrifice, able to face the upper spirits.
translations.idiomatic: He begins the suburban rite of paired sacrifice, fit to answer the spirits above.

translations.literal: This entire piece added and cut Xie's wording.
translations.idiomatic: This whole song revises Xie [Zhuang]'s text.

translations.literal: :: On the right, the evening-victim songs, both performed with repeats.
translations.idiomatic: :: Right: the evening-victim songs, each played twice.

translations.literal: Welcoming the spirits, they performed "Splendid Summer Music":
translations.idiomatic: To welcome the spirits they played "Zhao Xia" (Splendid Summer):

translations.literal: : Only the sage feasts the Emperor; only the filial feasts his kin.
translations.idiomatic: : The sage alone feasts God; the filial alone feasts his ancestors.

translations.literal: Below this, two lines were removed.
translations.idiomatic: Two lines below were cut.

translations.literal: Ritual proceeds with ancestral sacrifice; reverence reaches the suburban spirit-altar.
translations.idiomatic: Rites move through the ancestral temple; reverence extends to the suburban altar.

translations.literal: Golden branches planted at the center; broad music arrayed on four sides.
translations.idiomatic: Golden branches stand at the center; great music spreads on four sides.

translations.literal: Below this, eight lines were removed.
translations.idiomatic: Eight lines below were cut.

translations.literal: The moon carriage marks the beat; stars drive, supporting the wheel.
translations.idiomatic: The moon chariot sets the measure; stars urge on, steadying the wheel.

translations.literal: From afar they rise, the far chariot; brilliant, brilliant, in full array.
translations.idiomatic: They rise from afar, the distant carriages; bright and bright, in stately train.

translations.literal: Reporting completion, the great requital; receiving blessing from the primal spirit.
translations.idiomatic: The great report of completion is made; blessing is received from the primal spirit.

sentences.zh: 皇帝入壇東門，奏《永至之樂》：

translations.literal: When the emperor entered the altar's eastern gate, they performed "Music of Eternal Arrival":
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor entered the altar's east gate, they played "Music of Eternal Arrival":

translations.literal: :The purple altar gazes on the numinous; the green canopy awaits the spirit.
translations.idiomatic: :On the purple altar we gaze toward the sacred; beneath the green canopy we wait for the spirit.

translations.literal: Commanding heaven, presenting tribute; exhausting the earth, guests arrive.
translations.idiomatic: He draws heaven to his offering and the whole earth to his court.

translations.literal: Spirit gifts attend together; all reverence joins in blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit gifts come side by side; every rite merges into shared blessing.

translations.literal: Reverently manifesting inspection and feast; solemnly illuminating filial sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In reverence he shows himself for Heaven to see; in solemn light he honors the ancestral rite.

translations.literal: Awe enfolds the four numina; penetrating brilliance, the three luminaries.
translations.idiomatic: Majesty gathers the four spirits; radiance pierces sun, moon, and stars.

translations.literal: Imperial virtue wholly covers; great ritual flows in prosperity.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial virtue spreads everywhere; the great rite runs on in glory.

translations.literal: When the emperor ascended the altar, they performed the ascent-hymn lyrics:
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor mounted the altar, they sang the ascent hymn:

translations.literal: : Requital is only for serving Heaven; sacrifice truly honors the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: : Return is owed to Heaven alone; in sacrifice the spirits are truly exalted.

translations.literal: The scribe sets right the auspicious omen; the spirit dwells in lofty blessing.
translations.idiomatic: The historian fixes the lucky sign; the god abides in exalted grace.

translations.literal: The five altars display clear libation; the six honored ancestors array in ritual order.
translations.idiomatic: At the five shrines the fragrant wine shines; the six ancestors stand in due sequence.

translations.literal: Mount Fen looks to the dust; the imperial carriage solemnly rises.
translations.idiomatic: From Mount Fen they watch the imperial train; the royal chariot lifts in solemn state.

sentences.zh: 皇帝初獻，奏《文德宣烈之樂》：

translations.literal: At the emperor's first offering, they performed "Music of Civil Virtue Proclaiming Martial Glory":
translations.idiomatic: At the emperor's first offering they played "Music of Civil Virtue Proclaiming Martial Glory":

translations.literal: : Raising the great suburban altar, fixing Heaven's inmost heart.
translations.idiomatic: : He builds the great suburban mound and settles Heaven's true intent.

translations.literal: Thoughts and heart weave together; divination and planning accord.
translations.idiomatic: Mind and purpose align; oracle and counsel follow as one.

translations.literal: Below this, two lines were removed.
translations.idiomatic: Two lines below were cut.

translations.literal: Field candles set out; provisional fires linked.
translations.idiomatic: Torches stand in the fields; the signal fires run in line.

translations.literal: Great filial piety manifest; state ritual harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Great filial piety shines forth; the state rite flows as one.

sentences.zh: 此一句改，餘皆顏辭，此下又除二十二句。

translations.literal: This one line was changed; all the rest are Yan's wording; below this, twenty-two more lines were removed.
translations.idiomatic: One line was revised; the rest are Yan [Yanzhi]'s; twenty-two further lines below were cut.

translations.literal: Next they performed "Music of Martial Virtue Proclaiming Martial Glory":
translations.idiomatic: Next they played "Music of Martial Virtue Proclaiming Martial Glory":

translations.literal: : Merit lights the upper realm; virtue shines at heaven's center.
translations.idiomatic: : His merit illumines the heights; his virtue blazes at heaven's heart.

translations.literal: Winds shift through the nine domains; ritual adorns the eight borders.
translations.idiomatic: His influence moves the nine regions; his rites grace the eight reaches.

translations.literal: The four numina blaze at dawn; the five planets shine by night.
translations.idiomatic: The four spirits flame at morning; the five stars burn bright by night.

translations.literal: Receiving the calendar, founding the age; the Way flourishes in its former fame.
translations.idiomatic: He takes the mandate and binds the age; the Way grows rich with old renown.

sentences.zh: 太祖高皇帝配饗，奏《高德宣烈之樂》。

translations.literal: For the exalted ancestor, the High Emperor, in collateral feast, they performed "Music of Lofty Virtue Proclaiming Martial Glory."
translations.idiomatic: For the founding High Emperor in paired offering they played "Music of Lofty Virtue Proclaiming Martial Glory."

translations.literal: This piece was newly composed for the performance.
translations.idiomatic: This hymn was composed for the occasion.

translations.literal: Wording by Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Text by Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Jian.

translations.literal: : Feasting the Emperor, solemn with kin; aligning with Heaven, glory vast.
translations.idiomatic: : He feasts God in awe of his ancestors; matching Heaven, his glory spreads wide.

translations.literal: Successive through former ages; glory mirrors without outward limit.
translations.idiomatic: Line upon line from antiquity; honor reflects with nothing left outside.

translations.literal: Sun and moon spread splendor; minister-clouds stream in mist.
translations.idiomatic: Sun and moon pour forth their brilliance; auspicious clouds roll in haze.

translations.literal: The five Han shared repose; the six dark realms all at peace.
translations.idiomatic: The five Han knew the same rest; the six hidden worlds all found ease.

sentences.zh: 皇帝飲福酒，奏《嘉胙之樂》：

translations.literal: When the emperor drank the blessing wine, they performed "Music of Fine Blessing":
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor drank the blessing wine, they played "Music of Fine Blessing":

translations.literal: : Fine libation, fine ritual; receiving repose, receiving gifts.
translations.idiomatic: : Sweet wine and blessed rite; he takes rest and takes Heaven's gift.

sentences.zh: 盛德符景緯，昌華應帝策。

translations.literal: Abundant virtue matches the celestial markers; flourishing splendor answers the emperor's plan.
translations.idiomatic: Great virtue fits the signs in heaven; bright glory answers the emperor's design.

sentences.zh: 聖藹耀昌基，融祉暉世曆。

translations.literal: Sacred awe illumines the flourishing foundation; blended blessing shines through the age's calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Holy grace lights the thriving base; mingled blessing glows through the reign's years.

sentences.zh: 聲正涵月軌，書文騰日迹。

translations.literal: Sound set right embraces the moon's path; written pattern soars along the sun's track.
translations.idiomatic: True pitch holds the moon's course; written glory climbs the sun's trail.

sentences.zh: 寶瑞昭神圖，靈貺流瑞液。

translations.literal: Precious omens manifest the spirit-chart; spirit gifts flow as auspicious dew.
translations.idiomatic: Treasured signs reveal the divine chart; spirit bounty streams like lucky rain.

sentences.zh: 我皇崇暉祚，重芬冠往籍。

translations.literal: Our emperor exalts his radiant destiny; layered fragrance crowns past registers.
translations.idiomatic: Our emperor lifts his bright fortune; redoubled glory tops the records of old.

translations.literal: Sending off the spirits, they performed "Splendid Summer Music":
translations.idiomatic: To send off the spirits they played "Zhao Xia" (Splendid Summer):

translations.literal: : Offerings and feasting complete; ritual and music all in place.
translations.idiomatic: : Offerings and feast are full; rite and music meet in one.

translations.literal: The spirits' delight unfolds; the stellar banners turn back.
translations.idiomatic: The gods' pleasure opens wide; the starry flags wheel home.

translations.literal: Piercing the cloud-path; brushing the jade steps.
translations.idiomatic: They pierce the road of clouds; they skim the jade stair.

translations.literal: Purple vapor envelops; the azure sky opens.
translations.idiomatic: Purple mist gathers round; the blue heavens unfold.

translations.literal: Looking back on the imperial capital; gazing toward the jade terrace.
translations.idiomatic: They turn toward the royal city; they look back to the jade tower.

translations.literal: Leaving flourishing virtue; binding the sage's heart.
translations.idiomatic: They leave thriving grace behind; they seal the holy mind.

sentences.zh: 皇帝就燎位，奏《昭遠之樂》：

translations.literal: When the emperor took his position at the balefire, they performed "Music of Splendid Distance":
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor took his place at the pyre, they played "Music of Splendid Distance":

translations.literal: : Heaven descends with virtue; the Emperor returns with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: : Heaven sends down virtue; the emperor answers with rite.

translations.literal: Victim vessels set low before him; firewood and silks sent up to burn.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial vessels lie bowed before him; brushwood and silks rise into the flame.

translations.literal: The affair unfolds; the officer of harvest performs it; reverence reaches the fine jade and sweet grass.
translations.idiomatic: The rite runs its course through the harvest officer; reverence reaches the jade and fragrant herb.

translations.literal: Smoke offerings rise to the azure heavens; thunder rolls across the purple precinct.
translations.idiomatic: Offering smoke climbs to the blue sky; thunder shakes the purple altar-ground.

translations.literal: Fragrant offerings displayed, the written plan shown; solemn intent reaches the ancestral spirit-sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Sweet smoke is set forth, the oracle shown; solemn will reaches the ancestral offering.

translations.literal: Rites are not fulfilled by goods prepared; blessing is offered only through sincerity set forth.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual is not complete in offerings alone; fortune is granted only when sincerity is laid out.

sentences.zh: 皇帝還便殿，奏《休成之樂》，重奏。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned to the side hall, they performed "Music of Completed Rest," performed again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor withdrew to the side hall; "Music of Completed Rest" was played, then played again.

translations.literal: : Clearly serving the upper sacrifice, feast-offerings all set forth.
translations.idiomatic: : For the rites above, every offering is set out in order.

translations.literal: The returning chariot turns emerald; brushing the light, the imperial palaces soar.
translations.idiomatic: The returning carriage wheels in green; light brushes the soaring halls of the Son of Heaven.

translations.literal: Suspended bells spread in fullness; bronze stones shine blended.
translations.idiomatic: Frame-bells ring clear and wide; stone chimes blend in bright harmony.

translations.literal: Feather-pipes dazzle through deep hours; reed-flutes darken as they ride the wind.
translations.idiomatic: Feather pipes blaze through the long day; reed pipes murmur, carrying the wind along.

translations.literal: In the four sequences they pause measure; solemn rites halt the text.
translations.idiomatic: The ordered dances halt their pace; solemn ritual brings the script to rest.

translations.literal: Four metals tower as guards; six teams align their wheels.
translations.idiomatic: Four bronze bells stand as escort; six chariot teams keep their wheels in line.

translations.literal: :: On the right, southern suburban hymn texts.
translations.idiomatic: :: Right: southern suburban hymn texts.

translations.literal: [=] Section divider in the source text.
translations.idiomatic: [=] Section divider in the source text.

translations.literal: Northern Suburbs
translations.idiomatic: Northern Suburban Sacrifice

sentences.zh: =北郊樂歌辭，案《周頌·昊天有成命》，郊祀天地也。

translations.literal: Northern suburban music-and-dance lyrics: tracing Zhou Odes, "There Is the Decree of King," for suburban sacrifice to Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Lyrics for northern suburban music and dance—on the model of Zhou Odes, "There Is the Decree of King," for sacrificing to Heaven and Earth at the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 是則周、漢以來，祭天地皆同辭矣。

translations.literal: From Zhou and Han onward, sacrifices to Heaven and Earth all used the same wording.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhou and Han on, Heaven-and-Earth sacrifices shared the same texts.

sentences.zh: 宋顏延之《饗地神辭》一篇，餘與南郊同。

translations.literal: Song had one piece by Yan Yanzhi, "Hymn Feasting the Earth Spirit"; the rest matched the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: In Song, Yan Yanzhi's "Hymn to the Earth Spirit" stood alone; everything else matched the southern suburban set.

sentences.zh: 齊北郊羣臣入奏《肅咸樂》，牲入奏《引牲》，薦豆毛血奏《嘉薦》，皇帝入壇東門奏《永至》，飲福酒奏《嘉胙》，還便殿奏《休成》，辭竝與南郊同。

translations.literal: At Qi northern suburbs, when the multitude of ministers entered they played "Music of Solemn Awe"; when victims entered, "Music for Leading Victims"; when beans, hair, and blood were offered, "Music of Fine Offering"; when the emperor entered the altar's eastern gate, "Music of Eternal Arrival"; when drinking the blessing wine, "Music of Fine Flesh-Offering"; when returning to the side hall, "Music of Completed Rest"—the lyrics all matched the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: At the northern suburban rite in Qi: ministers entering heard "Solemn Awe"; victims entering, "Leading the Victims"; offering beans, hair, and blood, "Fine Offering"; the emperor at the altar's east gate, "Eternal Arrival"; the blessing wine, "Fine Flesh-Offering"; return to the side hall, "Completed Rest"—all with the same words as the southern suburb.

translations.literal: For welcoming and sending the spirits, "Splendid Summer" ascent hymns differed.
translations.idiomatic: Only the welcoming and sending pieces—"Zhao Xia" and the ascent hymns—differed.

translations.literal: Welcoming the earth spirit, they performed "Splendid Summer Music":
translations.idiomatic: To welcome the earth spirit they played "Zhao Xia":

translations.literal: : The edict honors ritual's high work; reverently feasting at the dark altar.
translations.idiomatic: : By edict ritual is exalted; in reverence one feasts at the dark altar.

translations.literal: The spirit sets right the cinnabar curtains; the moon is solemn on the purple steps.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit steadies the scarlet hangings; the moon stands grave on the purple terrace.

translations.literal: Spreading offerings, ascending splendor; wind-bells congeal in ringing clangor.
translations.idiomatic: Offerings are spread in splendor; wind-bells gather in steady chime.

translations.literal: The spirit alone arrives and halts; dense and distant, august.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit alone comes to rest—remote, august, and still.

translations.literal: Brightly gazing, the year's fragrance; circling the tour, the season's fullness.
translations.idiomatic: Brightly he watches the year's fragrance; in circuit he moves through the season's height.

translations.literal: Solemn indeed is honored ritual; spanning light, he holds the misty radiance.
translations.idiomatic: How solemn is the rite revered; he bears the hazy light across the sky.

translations.literal: When the emperor ascended the altar, the ascent hymn:
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor mounted the altar, the ascent hymn:

translations.literal: : Awaiting the spirit, reverently feasting; the suburban rite solemn, the patterned text.
translations.idiomatic: : He waits on the spirit and feasts in reverence; suburban rites are grave, the canonical text in order.

translations.literal: Suspended bells move, sound and bearing; offerings pure, victims fragrant.
translations.idiomatic: Frame-bells stir—sound and ceremony; clean offerings, sweet victims.

translations.literal: The yin powers thereby grant; the bright office thereby celebrates.
translations.idiomatic: The yin powers answer with gifts; the bright court marks the blessing.

translations.literal: The nine domains flourish in measure; the six grains show auspicious rightness.
translations.idiomatic: The nine regions thrive in good order; the six crops stand straight in auspicious season.

sentences.zh: 皇帝初獻，奏《地德凱容之樂》：

translations.literal: At the emperor's first offering, they performed "Music of Earthly Virtue, Triumphant Bearing":
translations.idiomatic: At the emperor's first offering they played "Earthly Virtue, Triumphant Bearing":

sentences.zh: :繕方丘，端國陰，掩圭晷，仰靈心。

translations.literal: : Repairing the square mound, rectifying the state's yin; covering the jade sundial, looking up to the spirit's heart.
translations.idiomatic: : He tends the square mound, sets the land's yin aright; covers the jade gnomon, lifts his heart to the spirit.

translations.literal: The edict's source winds through; everywhere over mound and grove.
translations.idiomatic: The edict's stream winds on, reaching every hill and wood.

sentences.zh: 此下除八句禮獻物，樂薦音。

translations.literal: Below this, eight lines on ritual offerings and music for presenting sound were removed.
translations.idiomatic: Eight lines below on ritual gifts and presentation music were cut.

sentences.zh: 此下除二十二句，餘皆顏辭。

translations.literal: Below this, twenty-two lines were removed; the rest are all Yan's wording.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-two lines below were cut; what remains is all Yan [Yanzhi].

translations.idiomatic: Empress Mu's maternal transforming grace is a matter apart from governance.

sentences.zh: 此二歌爲一章八句，別奏事御奉行。

translations.literal: These two songs are one chapter of eight lines each; they are to be performed separately as ceremonial officers carry out the rite.
translations.idiomatic: These two hymns are to be one eight-line chapter each, performed separately as the ceremony requires.

translations.literal: 」 An edict read 「Approved.」
translations.idiomatic: 」 The edict said 「Granted.」

sentences.zh: 尚書令王儉造太廟二室及郊配辭。

translations.literal: Minister Over the Masses Wang Jian composed hymn texts for two Imperial Ancestral Temple chambers and suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian, Minister Over the Masses, composed hymn texts for two ancestral-temple chambers and the suburban rite.

sentences.zh: 羣臣出入，奏《肅咸樂》歌辭：

translations.literal: As the multitude of ministers entered and exited, they played the lyrics of "Music of Solemn Awe":
translations.idiomatic: When ministers entered and left, they played "Music of Solemn Awe":

translations.literal: : Pure sincerity waves filial piety; filial feeling responds like smoke and frost.
translations.idiomatic: : Pure heart sways with filial grace; filial virtue answers through smoke and frost.

translations.literal: Proper rites adorn order; solemn ritual spreads wide.
translations.idiomatic: Due form adorns the sequence; solemn rites spread out wide.

translations.literal: Golden splendor arrays ornament; solemn wisdom rises in light.
translations.idiomatic: Gold brilliance sets out finery; grave wisdom flares with light.

translations.literal: Steady, steady the ascent music rises; stern, stern the tiered school hall.
translations.idiomatic: Deep and steady the ascending music; stern the terraced hall of learning.

translations.literal: Not pepper nor jade alone—they descend and are presented.
translations.idiomatic: Neither spice nor jade alone—they are brought down and offered up.

translations.literal: Earnestly expressing the spirit's heart; aiding and blessing, transmitting prosperity.
translations.idiomatic: Heartfelt reverence to the spirits; aid and blessing passed on in flourishing grace.

translations.literal: As victims entered and exited, they played the lyrics of "Music for Leading Victims":
translations.idiomatic: When victims were led in and out, they played "Music for Leading Victims":

translations.literal: : At sacrifice's start, honor the spirits; with reverent rite exalt the state.
translations.idiomatic: : At the rite's beginning, spirits are honored; with reverent ceremony the realm is exalted.

translations.literal: Extending reverence, spreading the ritual canon; binding filial piety, setting forth norms.
translations.idiomatic: Reverence reaches far; canon is spread abroad; filial duty binds; norms are displayed.

translations.literal: Fragrant cleansing is complete and solemn; sacrificial oxen are already prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Sweet ablutions done in solemn order; sacrificial beasts stand ready.

translations.literal: Upright sincerity flows in thought; proper bearing selects the auspicious light.
translations.idiomatic: Devotion rises, thought pours forth; formal bearing chooses the sacred hour.

translations.literal: Full rites wait through the night; continuous music awaits the dawn.
translations.idiomatic: The full rite holds through the night; unbroken music waits for dawn.

translations.literal: Honored mats for the emperor's scrutiny; to feast the bright spirits.
translations.idiomatic: High seats for the Son of Heaven to witness; to feast the luminous spirits.

sentences.zh: 薦豆呈毛血，奏《嘉薦樂》歌辭：

translations.literal: When beans, hair, and blood were offered, they played the lyrics of "Music of Fine Offering":
translations.idiomatic: When hair and blood on platters were presented, they played "Music of Fine Offering":

translations.literal: : Clear thoughts gleam distant; the sealed chamber is faint and dim.
translations.idiomatic: : Clear mind shines far; the inner chamber glows faint.

translations.literal: Reverent words carry feeling; solemn as if expecting.
translations.idiomatic: Reverent speech bears deep feeling; grave, as if hope were near.

translations.literal: Fragrant stands are fully set out; fine offerings arrayed together.
translations.idiomatic: Sweet-smelling trays stand full; choice offerings line the hall.

translations.literal: Condensed fragrance wafts in smoke; divided light, stars shine clear.
translations.idiomatic: Thick incense curls in smoke; starlight splits bright and clear.

translations.literal: Wise spirits descend in proper manner; harmonizing with our imperial way.
translations.idiomatic: Bright spirits come down as they should; they align with the imperial path.

translations.literal: Above, clarifying the five cords; below, transforming the eight directions.
translations.idiomatic: Above, the five cords are clarified; below, the eight reaches are molded.

translations.literal: :: Right: evening-victim hymn texts.
translations.idiomatic: :: Right: evening-victim hymn texts.

translations.literal: Welcoming the spirits, they played the lyrics of "Splendid Summer Music":
translations.idiomatic: To welcome the spirits they played "Splendid Summer Music":

translations.literal: : Choosing day and hour, selecting qi; unfolding the rite with reverent respect.
translations.idiomatic: : A sacred day is chosen, qi is selected; the rite unfolds in reverent awe.

translations.literal: Double gates moon-bright hollow; layered windows spread smoke.
translations.idiomatic: Double doors hollow with moonlight; tiered windows breathe ritual smoke.

translations.literal: Bearing empty jade libation; bearing received golden branches.
translations.idiomatic: Empty jade cups are carried; golden branches are received.

translations.literal: Heaven's song breaks off the feast; cloud dance exhausts the ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's hymn ends the offering; cloud-dance completes the rite.

translations.literal: The spirits alone descend and halt; floating light, condensing dawn.
translations.idiomatic: The spirits descend and rest; light spreads, dawn-glow gathers.

translations.literal: Imperial splendor forever lush; dissolved ornament spreads its pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial glory ever verdant; flowing ornament spreads its weave.

sentences.zh: 皇帝入廟北門，奏《永至樂》歌辭：

translations.literal: When the emperor entered the temple's north gate, they played the lyrics of "Music of Eternal Arrival":
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor entered the temple north gate, they played "Music of Eternal Arrival":

translations.literal: : Yu of Xia's counsel is the model; Zhou's canon sets order.
translations.idiomatic: : The counsel of Yu is the rule; Zhou's classic sets the sequence.

translations.literal: Nine offices join in affairs; eight directions bear the canopy.
translations.idiomatic: Nine bureaus join in duty; eight quarters uphold the realm.

translations.literal: Imperial guard stands quietly arrayed; slow music is fully raised.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial escort stands in silent order; leisurely music lifts throughout.

translations.literal: Fixed tassels as if in longing; tilted jade roundels, standing poised.
translations.idiomatic: Pendants hang still as in yearning; jade pendants tilt, the bearer stands waiting.

translations.literal: Vigorous, vigorous the jade guards; grave, grave the ritual bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Steady, steady the jade escort; solemn, solemn the ritual mien.

translations.literal: Bearing imperial grace in the royal step; spreading the emperor's track.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial grace marks the royal pace; the Son of Heaven's path is traced out.

translations.literal: The Grand Invocator poured libation on the ground; they played the ascent hymn lyrics:
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Invocator poured libation on the earth and sang the ascent hymn:

translations.literal: : When pure and bright, libation is already prepared; great filial piety then flourishes.
translations.idiomatic: : Libation stands pure and ready; great filial piety shines forth.

translations.literal: Heavenly rite shows gentle sorrow; the emperor's heart is solemn in thought.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's rite wears gentle mien; the emperor's heart stands grave in thought.

translations.literal: Already fragrant are the room vessels and beans; then the sacrificial victim is cleansed.
translations.idiomatic: Room vessels and beans already sweet with scent; the sacrificial ox is washed pure.

translations.literal: Fragrant libation rises in the rite; jade bells sound the ascent hymn.
translations.idiomatic: Spiced libation rises in ritual; jade bells lift the ascent hymn.

translations.literal: Richly confronting the dim solemnity; thereby honoring the numinous spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Richly they meet the hidden solemn shrine; thus they serve the numinous spirit.

translations.literal: To feast and to sacrifice—only feeling, only sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: They offer and they sacrifice—pure feeling, pure sincerity.

sentences.zh: 皇祖廣陵丞府君神室奏《凱容樂》歌辭：

translations.literal: Imperial Grandfather Lord Guangling Assistant Magistrate's spirit chamber performed the hymn text of "Triumphant Appearance Music":
translations.idiomatic: At Imperial Grandfather Lord Guangling Assistant Magistrate's spirit chamber they played the "Triumphant Appearance" hymn:

translations.literal: : The state is manifest and flourishing; imperial solemnity is exalted.
translations.idiomatic: : State glory stands full and bright; imperial reverence rises supreme.

translations.literal: Fortune ascends, threads reach far; ages founded, bright harmony blends.
translations.idiomatic: Blessings mount and omens reach far; founding ages blend in radiant accord.

translations.literal: Profuse the wise lineage; luxuriant the royal culture.
translations.idiomatic: Wise threads weave a rich lineage; royal grace spreads lush and wide.

translations.literal: Bright advances its beginning; deep wisdom its cultural end.
translations.idiomatic: Bright at the first advance; deep wisdom at the last flourish.

sentences.zh: 皇祖太中大夫府君神室奏《凱容樂》歌辭：

translations.literal: Imperial Grandfather Lord Grand Master for All Purposes' spirit chamber performed the hymn text of "Triumphant Appearance Music":
translations.idiomatic: At Imperial Grandfather Lord Grand Master for All Purposes' spirit chamber they played the "Triumphant Appearance" hymn:

translations.literal: : Jade branches flourish deep; jade spring shines clear and deep.
translations.idiomatic: : Jade branches bloom in deep profusion; the jade spring shines clear from its source.

translations.literal: Great is the imperial achievement; it thrusts forth bright strength.
translations.idiomatic: Great the imperial achievement; bright strength thrusts forth.

translations.literal: Forever speak reverent thought; thereby reverent in teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Forever they speak in reverent thought; thus reverent in teaching.

translations.literal: The good path, excellent governance; glory has brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: A good road and fair governance; glory shines abroad.

sentences.zh: 皇祖淮陰令府君神室奏《凱容樂》歌辭：

translations.literal: Imperial Grandfather Lord Huaiyin Magistrate's spirit chamber performed the hymn text of "Triumphant Appearance Music":
translations.idiomatic: At Imperial Grandfather Lord Huaiyin Magistrate's spirit chamber they played the "Triumphant Appearance" hymn:

translations.literal: : Stern the ancestral temple, correct the rites; exalted the feast, beginning the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: : Solemn ancestral rites stand set aright; the exalted feast opens sacrifice.

translations.literal: The nine chapters already adorned; the three pure already displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Nine ritual regalia stand adorned; the Three Pure are already set out.

translations.literal: Manifest reverence to the imperial ancestor; receiving and invoking the numinous spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Bright reverence to the imperial forebear; they receive the numinous spirit.

translations.literal: Steadfast blessing thus accorded; harmonious ministers are neighbors.
translations.idiomatic: Steadfast blessing keeps all in accord; harmony dwells among the officers.

sentences.zh: 皇曾祖卽丘令府君神室奏《凱容樂》歌辭：

translations.literal: Imperial Great-Grandfather Lord Jiqiu Magistrate's spirit chamber performed the hymn text of "Triumphant Appearance Music":
translations.idiomatic: At Imperial Great-Grandfather Lord Jiqiu Magistrate's spirit chamber they played the "Triumphant Appearance" hymn:

translations.literal: : Solemn and reverent the sacrifice; pure the service, fragrant offerings blended.
translations.idiomatic: : Sole reverence marks the sacrifice; pure service blends fragrant offerings.

translations.literal: Ringed robes and image ornaments; finely woven silk and reed pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual robes circle in ornament; fine silk and reed pipes fill the hall.

translations.literal: Bright, bright the illustrious ancestor; still bestowed dragon glory.
translations.idiomatic: Bright, bright the heroic forebear; dragon glory is still conferred.

translations.literal: Like the "Ya" in Zhou; as the "Song" in Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Like the "Ya" hymns among the Ji; like the "Song" hymns in Shang.

sentences.zh: 皇祖太常卿府君神室奏《凱容樂》歌辭：

translations.literal: Imperial Grandfather Lord Minister of Ceremonies' spirit chamber performed the hymn text of "Triumphant Appearance Music":
translations.idiomatic: At Imperial Grandfather Lord Minister of Ceremonies' spirit chamber they played the "Triumphant Appearance" hymn:

translations.literal: : Spirit palace flourishes in splendor; bright chamber, flourishing foundation.
translations.idiomatic: : The spirit hall flourishes in splendor; bright shrine, thriving foundation.

translations.literal: Virtue gathers in feather ornaments; the Way's libation in composed wording.
translations.idiomatic: Virtue gathers like plumed regalia; the Way's libation shapes the hymn.

translations.literal: Lend me the imperial lineage; excellent is my imperial continuity.
translations.idiomatic: Grant me the imperial thread; glorious is the royal line.

translations.literal: Manifest and great its years; the state's unity, its fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Bright and vast its age; unified realm, abounding fortune.

sentences.zh: 皇考宣皇神室奏《宣德凱容樂》歌辭：

translations.literal: Imperial Father Emperor Xuan's spirit chamber performed the hymn text of "Virtue-Proclaiming Triumphant Appearance Music":
translations.idiomatic: At Imperial Father Emperor Xuan's spirit chamber they played the "Virtue-Proclaiming Triumphant Appearance" hymn:

translations.literal: : The Way threaded through its appointed destiny; righteousness opens stored virtue for use.
translations.idiomatic: : The Way is spun through destined times; righteousness opens hidden virtue to use.

translations.literal: Augment the wise ancestor; utmost, thereby unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: How august the wise forebear; utmost is his free sway.

translations.literal: Following the rule, blazing illumination; inheriting the square, redoubled fragrance.
translations.idiomatic: He follows the compass in blazing light; he inherits the square in doubled fragrance.

translations.literal: Virtue overflows Xuanyuan and Fuxi; the Way flourishes like fiery clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Virtue overflows Yellow Emperor and Fuxi; the Way flourishes like fiery clouds.

sentences.zh: 昭皇后神室奏《凱容樂》歌辭：

translations.literal: Empress Zhao's spirit chamber performed the hymn text of "Triumphant Appearance Music":
translations.idiomatic: At Empress Zhao's spirit chamber they played the "Triumphant Appearance" hymn:

translations.literal: : Moon spirit bears celebration; cloud omens open fortune.
translations.idiomatic: : The moon spirit brings blessed birth; cloud omens open good fortune.

translations.literal: The Way is luxuriant, deep and gentle; virtue displayed in emblem.
translations.idiomatic: The Way stands deep and gently rich; virtue shows in noble emblem.

translations.literal: Pure teaching within the palace; model form beyond the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Pure teaching within the palace reaches; her model form spreads beyond the cosmos.

translations.literal: Bearing and dance congealed in splendor; golden feather dance transmits harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Graceful bearing gathers flower-like splendor; golden feather dance spreads gentle harmony.

sentences.zh: 皇帝還東壁上福酒，奏《永祚樂》歌辭：

translations.literal: The emperor returned to the east wall to place blessing wine; they played the lyrics of "Everlasting Fortune Music":
translations.idiomatic: The emperor returned to the east wall to offer blessing wine; they played "Everlasting Fortune Music":

translations.literal: : Building the palace, eaves raised high; joining axles, culture aligned.
translations.idiomatic: : The palace rises, eaves lifted high; realms join axle to axle in shared rites.

translations.literal: Ten thousand spirits then overflow; hundred rites thereby abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Myriad spirits fill the hall; a hundred rites stand full and rich.

translations.literal: Red strings wind around the breeze; green feathers halt the clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Red strings curl through the wind; green plumes hold the clouds in pause.

translations.literal: Cassia cups already washed; jade stands already fragrant.
translations.idiomatic: Cassia goblets are washed pure; jade stands sweet with incense.

translations.literal: Ascending offerings with only sincerity; manifest rites with only fragrance.
translations.idiomatic: They offer with pure sincerity; rites shine sweet with fragrance.

translations.literal: Blessing descends on distant posterity; fortune gathered in swirling mist.
translations.idiomatic: Blessing falls on distant heirs; fortune gathers in misty swirls.

translations.literal: Sending off the spirits, they played the lyrics of "Si Xia Music":
translations.idiomatic: Sending off the spirits, they played "Si Xia Music":

translations.literal: : Rite already completed; music thereby brings joy.
translations.idiomatic: : Rite rises complete; music brings delight.

translations.literal: Bright rites overflow; spirit feasts have yet more.
translations.idiomatic: Bright rites spill over; the spirit-feast lingers on.

translations.literal: Human and spirit share libation; reverent teaching spreads.
translations.idiomatic: Mortals and spirits share libation; reverent teaching goes abroad.

translations.literal: Extended light stirs; the spirit carriage soars.
translations.idiomatic: Light stretches forth; the spirit chariot takes flight.

translations.literal: Fragrance fills the nine borderlands; mirrors the eight directions.
translations.idiomatic: Fragrance fills the nine reaches; blessing mirrors the eight directions.

translations.literal: Blessing knows no bound; fortune knows no end.
translations.idiomatic: Blessing has no limit; the throne has no end.

sentences.zh: 皇帝詣便殿，奏《休成樂》歌辭：

translations.literal: The emperor proceeded to the side hall and performed the hymn text of "Completion and Rest Music":
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went to the side hall and played the "Xiucheng" hymn:

translations.literal: : Wise filial piety performs libation; feast-reverence reaches everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: : Wise filial piety pours libation; feast and reverence fill every place.

translations.literal: Solemn mien pauses the sequence; dance-text stills the suspended bells.
translations.idiomatic: Grave mien stills the rite; dance and bells fall quiet.

translations.literal: Morning rites raise the halting; night guard floats the imperial bell.
translations.idiomatic: Morning ceremony halts the march; night guards float the royal bells.

translations.literal: Tasseled curtains spread like clouds; emerald banners wheel in splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Canopy curtains billow like clouds; imperial banners wheel in light.

translations.literal: Reverently considering exalted merit; bright governance woven again.
translations.idiomatic: Reverently honoring lofty worth; bright rule is woven anew.

translations.literal: State design reaches far in abundance; flourishing plan is then proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: State design spreads far and wide; the plan for prosperity is proclaimed.

translations.literal: Imperial Ancestral Temple ascent hymn texts, two chapters:
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Ancestral Temple ascent hymns, two chapters:

translations.literal: : The king establishes the state; sets temple and gathers spirits.
translations.idiomatic: : The king founds the realm; he builds the temple and gathers the spirits.

translations.literal: Monthly offerings follow the canon; seasonal rites follow the bright measure.
translations.idiomatic: Monthly offerings follow ancient canon; seasonal rites mark the bright calendar.

translations.literal: Gazing at the time with hidden thought; rain and dew pursue heartfelt feeling.
translations.idiomatic: They mark the season with hidden reverence; grace like rain and dew follows deep feeling.

translations.literal: Choosing the day, divining the gnomon; solemn offering raises the text.
translations.idiomatic: Day is chosen, gnomon cast; the sealed offering raises the written rite.

translations.literal: Golden vessels steeped with cassia; inner canopy spreads incense.
translations.idiomatic: Gold goblets steep with cassia; the inner canopy breathes incense.

translations.literal: Officials prepared in solemn array; halting splendor, opening clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Officers stand prepared in solemn ranks; splendor pauses as clouds part.

translations.literal: : Ultimate feast reaches the utmost; wise filial piety, earnest rites.
translations.idiomatic: : The feast reaches its height; wise filial piety keeps the rites in earnest.

translations.literal: All offerings wholly pure; sound and fragrance join as one.
translations.idiomatic: Every offering is pure; music and incense are one.

translations.literal: Qi bright supports the dark realm; distant yearning entwines the far.
translations.idiomatic: Bright breath upholds the hidden realm; distant yearning binds the far.

translations.literal: Welcoming strings in startled haste; successive dancers linger till evening.
translations.idiomatic: Strings sound in urgent welcome; dancers in turn hold the evening.

translations.literal: The sage heart treads and waits; seasons change, sorrow grows.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's heart keeps watch; the seasons turn and sorrow deepens.

translations.literal: Subtle feeling lofty and deep; splendid emblem ever brighter.
translations.idiomatic: Subtle feeling runs deep; the noble emblem shines ever brighter.

sentences.zh: 太祖高皇帝神室奏《高德宣烈樂》歌辭：

translations.literal: Grand Ancestor Emperor Gaozu's spirit chamber performed the hymn text of "Lofty Virtue Proclaims Martial Glory Music":
translations.idiomatic: At Grand Ancestor Gaozu's spirit chamber they played the "Lofty Virtue Proclaims Martial Glory" hymn:

translations.literal: : In long dark beginnings; solemn was the governance.
translations.idiomatic: : Long in primal darkness; solemn the grand design.

translations.literal: Both civil and martial; both sage and divine.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and martial alike; sage and divine alike.

translations.literal: In motion he pacified crisis and chaos; at rest he drew close to the people.
translations.idiomatic: In action he stilled crisis and chaos; at rest he drew the people near.

translations.literal: He received the bright mandate; he suddenly held the eight reaches.
translations.idiomatic: He received the bright mandate; all the eight reaches were his.

translations.literal: Grasping fate he began destiny; brightly he opened Yu's realm.
translations.idiomatic: He seized the pivot and began the mandate; he brightly opened the realm of Yu.

translations.literal: Righteousness filled heaven's depths; rites shone on earth's axis.
translations.idiomatic: Righteousness filled heaven's deep; rites lit earth's axis.

translations.literal: Grace none did not embrace; awe none did not reverence.
translations.idiomatic: None went ungraced; none failed to stand in awe.

translations.literal: Barbarians exhausted joy; elephants came bearing fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Tribes bowed in full submission; elephants came bearing blessing.

translations.literal: Wind subsides, transformation shaped; bright sun spreads auspicious signs.
translations.idiomatic: Winds lay down and change took shape; the bright sun spread good omens.

translations.literal: Trustworthy stars hold radiance; black millet flows with fragrance.
translations.idiomatic: Stars hold their bright trust; sacred millet spreads its fragrance.

translations.literal: Seven temples observe virtue; six musics proclaim the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Seven temples display his virtue; six kinds of music proclaim his glory.

translations.literal: Reverence first, reverence always; feast and offer we do.
translations.idiomatic: Reverence before all else—we feast and we serve.

sentences.zh: 穆皇后神室奏《穆德凱容之樂》歌辭：

translations.literal: Empress Mu's spirit chamber performed the hymn text of "Mude Kairong Music":
translations.idiomatic: At Empress Mu's spirit chamber they played the "Mude Kairong" hymn:

translations.literal: : Great Si became Zhou's consort; at Mount Tu she matched Yu.
translations.idiomatic: : Great Si wed Zhou; at Mount Tu she matched Yu.

translations.literal: Our empress inherited emblems; stacked rules and measures.
translations.idiomatic: Our empress inherited noble virtue; rule upon rule, measure upon measure.

translations.literal: Solemn, solemn the spirit palace; soaring, soaring the "Cloud Dance."
translations.idiomatic: Grave and solemn the sealed palace; soaring, soaring "Cloud Dance."

translations.literal: Feasting makes virtue fragrant; without cease through all time.
translations.idiomatic: Feast brings fragrant virtue; it will never end through all ages.

sentences.zh: 高宗明皇帝神室奏《明德凱容之樂》歌辭：

translations.literal: Emperor Ming's spirit chamber performed the hymn text of "Mingde Kairong Music":
translations.idiomatic: At Emperor Ming's spirit chamber they played the "Mingde Kairong" hymn:

translations.literal: : Many hardships fortified the enterprise; deep sorrow awakened the sage.
translations.idiomatic: : Hardship after hardship built the throne; deep care awakened the sage.

translations.literal: Imperial lineage continued martial virtue; at the time he held to striving.
translations.idiomatic: The royal house carried on martial worth; in his day he strove with all his might.

translations.literal: Willow rises, bearing auspicious signs; a hundred walls rise in praise.
translations.idiomatic: The rising willow brought good omen; a hundred walls rose in song.

translations.literal: Righteous though honoring Xia; merit matched receiving the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Though he honored the Xia sages, his merit fit Heaven's mandate.

translations.literal: Far none did not come in loyalty; near none did not keep reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Far and near, all came in loyalty; all kept reverence.

translations.literal: His bearing orderly; his mien reverent.
translations.idiomatic: His bearing was orderly; his mien was reverent.

translations.literal: Glorious is the sovereign's facing; bright is the succession and office.
translations.idiomatic: Glorious his rule as lord; bright the line he inherits.

translations.literal: Truly the king is the lord; he receives this abundant blessing.
translations.idiomatic: True king and true lord—he wins these ample blessings.

translations.literal: Rite is used to display service; music is used to move spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Rite makes the service plain; music moves the spirits.

translations.literal: Eight gui vessels are arrayed in the chamber; six dances fill the court.
translations.idiomatic: Eight grain-vessels fill the hall; six rows of dance fill the yard.

translations.literal: View virtue in the temple; emblemize virtue in form.
translations.idiomatic: Virtue is seen in the temple; virtue is shown in outward form.

translations.literal: Four seas come to sacrifice; ten thousand states all find peace.
translations.idiomatic: The four seas come to offer sacrifice; every realm knows peace.

translations.literal: [=] Section divider in the source text.
translations.idiomatic: [=] Section divider in the source text.

translations.literal: Field-Ploughing Rite
translations.idiomatic: Field-Ploughing Rite

sentences.zh: =藉田歌辭，漢章帝，玄武司馬班固奏用《周頌·載芟》祠先農。

translations.literal: = Field-ploughing hymn texts: Emperor Zhang of Han—Marshal of the Black Tortoise Ban Gu memorialized using Zhou Odes "Weeding" to sacrifice to the Prior Farmer.
translations.idiomatic: = Field-ploughing hymn texts: under Han Zhangdi, Marshal of the Black Tortoise Ban Gu submitted that the Zhou Ode "Weeding" be used to sacrifice to the Prior Farmer.

sentences.zh: 晉傅玄作《祀先農先蠶夕牲歌詩》一篇八句，《迎送神》一篇，《饗社稷》、《先農》、《先聖》、《先蠶歌詩》三篇，前一篇十二句，中一篇十六句，後一篇十二句，辭皆敘田農事。

translations.literal: In Jin, Fu Xuan composed "Evening Victim Hymn-Poem for Sacrifice to Prior Farmer and Prior Silkworm" one piece of eight lines; "Welcoming and Sending Spirits" one piece; "Feasting Altar of Soil and Grain," "Prior Farmer," "Prior Sage," and "Prior Silkworm Hymn-Poems" three pieces—the first twelve lines, the middle sixteen lines, the last twelve lines—all texts narrate field and farming matters.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin, Fu Xuan wrote one eight-line "Evening Victim Hymn for Sacrifices to Prior Farmer and Prior Silkworm," one "Welcoming and Sending Spirits," and three hymn-poems—"Feasting the Altar of Soil and Grain," "Prior Farmer," and "Prior Sage and Prior Silkworm"—of twelve, sixteen, and twelve lines, all describing field and farming affairs.

sentences.zh: 胡道安《先農饗神詩》一篇，竝八句。

translations.literal: Hu Dao'an's "Prior Farmer Spirit-Feasting Poem" one piece, also eight lines.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Dao'an's "Prior Farmer Spirit-Feasting Poem," likewise eight lines.

translations.literal: The Music Bureau transmitted three old song chapters.
translations.idiomatic: The Music Bureau handed down three old song chapters.

sentences.zh: 藉田，詔驍騎將軍江淹造《藉田歌》。

translations.literal: Field-ploughing rite: an edict ordered General of Resolute Cavalry Jiang Yan to compose "Field-Ploughing Song."
translations.idiomatic: For the field-ploughing rite, an edict ordered General of Resolute Cavalry Jiang Yan to compose "Field-Ploughing Song."

sentences.zh: 淹制二章，不依胡、傅，世祖口勑付太樂歌之。

translations.literal: Yan composed two chapters, not following Hu and Fu; the Founding Emperor by oral command had the Grand Music Office sing them.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yan wrote two chapters, not following Hu or Fu; Emperor Shizu by spoken edict had the Grand Music Office set them to song.

translations.literal: Sacrifice to Prior Farmer, welcoming and sending spirits ascent hymn:
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice to the Prior Farmer—welcoming and sending spirits ascent hymn:

translations.literal: : Feathered canopy follows in motion; golden carriage roams in season.
translations.idiomatic: : Feathered regalia moves in train; the golden chariot roams at the season.

translations.literal: Teaching rises as a mirror of righteousness; music threads together, rites perfected.
translations.idiomatic: Teaching soars, a mirror of right principle; music and rite are woven complete.

translations.literal: First leads the red paired oxen; in person follows the green fields.
translations.idiomatic: He leads the red yoked pair; himself he treads the green furrows.

translations.literal: Spirit—holy spirit; the year is abundant, blessing gentle.
translations.idiomatic: O spirit, sacred spirit—the year grows rich, grace turns soft.

translations.literal: Spirit-feasting hymn texts:
translations.idiomatic: Hymn text for feasting the spirits:

translations.literal: : Jade goblets already adorned; embroidered gui vessels are displayed.
translations.idiomatic: : Jade cups are arrayed in glory; broidered grain-vessels stand displayed.

translations.literal: Now preparing fine seed; forever nourishing the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Fine seed is cooked in due rite; forever it feeds the people's toil.

translations.literal: [=] Section divider in the source text.
translations.idiomatic: [=] Section divider in the source text.

translations.literal: New Year's Grand Assembly
translations.idiomatic: New Year's Grand Assembly

sentences.zh: =元會大饗四廂樂歌辭，晉太僕傅玄撰。

translations.literal: = New Year's grand feast four-gallery music hymn texts, Jin Grand Master of the Household Fu Xuan composed.
translations.idiomatic: = New Year's Grand Assembly feast music for the four galleries, composed by Jin Grand Master of the Household Fu Xuan.

sentences.zh: 正旦大會行禮歌詩四章，壽酒詩一章，食舉東西廂樂十三章，黃門郎張華作。

translations.literal: New Year's Day grand assembly ceremonial hymn-poems four chapters, longevity wine poem one chapter, food-raising east-west gallery music thirteen chapters, Yellow Gate Gentleman Zhang Hua composed.
translations.idiomatic: For the New Year's Day grand assembly: four ceremonial hymn-poems, one longevity-wine poem, and thirteen food-raising gallery pieces east and west, by Yellow Gate Gentleman Zhang Hua.

sentences.zh: 上壽食舉行禮詩十八章，中書監荀勗、侍郎成公綏，言數各異。

translations.literal: Longevity presentation and food-raising ceremonial poems eighteen chapters, Secretariat Director Xun Xu and Attendant-in-Ordinary Cheng Gong-sui—the line counts each differ.
translations.idiomatic: Eighteen hymn-poems for longevity presentation and food-raising were credited to Secretariat Director Xun Xu and Attendant-in-Ordinary Cheng Gong-sui, but with differing line counts.

sentences.zh: 宋黃門郎王韶之造《肆夏》四章，行禮一章，上壽一章，登歌三章，食舉十章，《前後舞歌》一章。

translations.literal: Song Yellow Gate Gentleman Wang Shao-zhi made "Si Xia" four chapters, ceremonial one chapter, longevity presentation one chapter, ascent hymns three chapters, food-raising ten chapters, "Front and Rear Dance Song" one chapter.
translations.idiomatic: In Song, Yellow Gate Gentleman Wang Shao-zhi composed four "Si Xia" chapters, one ceremonial piece, one longevity presentation, three ascent hymns, ten food-raising pieces, and one "Front and Rear Dance Song."

translations.literal: Qi slightly reformed, mostly retaining old texts.
translations.idiomatic: Qi made slight revisions, largely keeping the old wording.

translations.literal: Its "Front and Rear Dance" two chapters newly revised.
translations.idiomatic: Its two "Front and Rear Dance" chapters were newly rewritten.

sentences.zh: 其臨軒樂，亦奏《肆夏·於鑠》四章。

translations.literal: Its facing-the-gallery music also performed "Si Xia: Imposing Splendor" four chapters.
translations.idiomatic: For music at the facing-the-gallery audience, four chapters of "Si Xia: Imposing Splendor" were also played.

translations.literal: The hymn text of "Si Xia Music":
translations.idiomatic: "Si Xia Music" hymn text:

translations.literal: : Imposing is our emperor, embodying benevolence and embracing the Origin.
translations.idiomatic: : Imposing is our emperor, his person benevolence and the primal origin bound together.

translations.literal: Qi bright as sun and moon, matching glory with Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Clear as sun and moon; his light matches Heaven and Earth.

translations.literal: Pottery-molds the hundred kings, examining Yellow Xu as standard.
translations.idiomatic: He molds the hundred kings; Yellow Thearch is his measure.

translations.literal: Great design settles the mandate; reports at dawn to the four border lands.
translations.idiomatic: Grand counsel fixes the mandate; at the hour he announces it to the four marches.

translations.literal: :: Right: one piece—guests enter; the four galleries play.
translations.idiomatic: :: Right: one movement—guests enter; all four galleries play.

translations.literal: : Stately, stately border lords; winged, winged host of officials.
translations.idiomatic: : Stately come the frontier lords; close-ranked the host of officers.

translations.literal: Full dress awaiting dawn; at bright departure they come to court.
translations.idiomatic: In full dress they wait for dawn; at first light they arrive at court.

translations.literal: Feasted with eight delicacies; music with "Nine Shao."
translations.idiomatic: They feast on eight rare dishes; music is the "Nine Shao."

translations.literal: Looking up in reverence to the heavenly countenance; their plans greatly displayed.
translations.idiomatic: They look up in awe to the imperial face; their counsel shines clear.

translations.literal: :: Right: one piece—the emperor faces south; the four galleries play.
translations.idiomatic: :: Right: one movement—the emperor faces south; all four galleries play.

sentences.zh: 皇帝入變服，四廂幷奏前二曲。

translations.literal: Emperor enters and changes dress; the four galleries together perform the first two pieces.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor enters and changes his robes; all four galleries play the first two movements together.

translations.literal: : Legal statutes already set; the first banquet long unfolds.
translations.idiomatic: : The court statutes are set; the opening banquet spreads long.

translations.literal: Numerous, numerous arrayed feudatories; upright robes on the imperial hall steps.
translations.idiomatic: Princes rank in splendor; formal dress fills the imperial hall.

translations.literal: Drinking harmony without excess; august bearing has surplus.
translations.idiomatic: They drink in harmony without excess; dignity and bearing have room to spare.

translations.literal: Warm and respectful in their posts; reverence to the end as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle and reverent in their seats; to the end they keep the first awe.

translations.literal: : Nine merits already sung; six generations only at their time.
translations.idiomatic: : The nine achievements are sung; the six ages are timely hailed.

translations.literal: Clothed in virtue through music; proclaiming the Way through poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Grace is worn in music; the Way is preached in song.

translations.literal: Solemn is the great harmony; all things equally flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Solemn the great harmony; every kind of thing thrives as one.

translations.literal: Accumulated celebration from afar; accomplishment is announced here.
translations.idiomatic: Blessings piled since long ago—today the work is declared done.

sentences.zh: ::右二曲，皇帝入變服，黃鐘太蔟二廂奏。

translations.literal: :: Right: two pieces—the emperor enters and changes dress; the Yellow Bell and Greater Cluster galleries play.
translations.idiomatic: :: Right: two movements—the emperor enters to change his robes; the Yellow Bell and Greater Cluster galleries perform.

translations.literal: Grand assembly ceremonial hymn texts:
translations.idiomatic: Hymn text for the grand assembly rite:

sentences.zh: :大哉皇齊，長發其祥：祚隆姬夏，道邁虞唐。

translations.literal: : How great is Imperial Qi; long has fortune flourished: eminence surpasses Ji and Xia, the Way outpaces Yu and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: : Great is imperial Qi; good fortune flows from a distant line—its throne outshines the houses of Ji and Xia, its Way surpasses Yu and Tang.

translations.literal: Its virtue is bright and penetrating; blessed is its blazing glory.
translations.idiomatic: Virtue shines clear within it; grace and blazing glory attend.

translations.literal: Matching Heaven as pole; the stars dwell in the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Paired with Heaven as cosmic pole, its power fills the four directions.

sentences.zh: :皇矣我后，聖德通靈：有命自天，誕授休禎。

translations.literal: : August is our sovereign; holy virtue reaches the spirits: mandate comes from Heaven, granting this blessed omen.
translations.idiomatic: : August is our lord and queen—sacred virtue touches the unseen; Heaven sends the mandate and bestows this blessed sign.

translations.literal: The dragon soars at purple zenith, founding our Qi capital;
translations.idiomatic: The dragon rises at purple pole-star height and builds our Qi capital;

translations.literal: Light fills the cosmos; glorious, luminous.
translations.idiomatic: Its radiance houses all under heaven—splendid, bright, and clear.

translations.literal: :: Right: two pieces—the Gu Xian gallery plays.
translations.idiomatic: :: Right: two movements—the Gu Xian gallery performs.

translations.literal: Longevity presentation hymn text:
translations.idiomatic: Hymn for presenting the cup of longevity:

translations.literal: : Present the longevity cup; celebrate the holy emperor.
translations.idiomatic: : We raise the cup of long life and hail the sacred sovereign.

sentences.zh: 靈祚窮二儀，休明等三光。

translations.literal: Spirit-blessing reaches the two principles; glory equals the three luminaries.
translations.idiomatic: Sacred fortune spans earth and sky; its splendor rivals sun, moon, and stars.

translations.literal: :: Right: one piece—the Yellow Bell gallery plays.
translations.idiomatic: :: Right: one movement—the Yellow Bell gallery performs.

translations.literal: Before-the-hall ascent hymn text:
translations.idiomatic: Ascent hymn before the hall:

translations.literal: : Bright is the state of Qi; the imperial Way is gathered and glorious.
translations.idiomatic: : Bright is the realm of Qi; the imperial Way is gathered in radiance.

translations.literal: Patterning Heaven, it spreads transformation; light fixes the Heavenly Protection.
translations.idiomatic: It takes Heaven as model and sends transformation abroad; its radiance secures the Heavenly Mandate.

translations.literal: Once Heavenly Protection is fixed, all directions come to audience.
translations.idiomatic: When the Mandate is fixed, the myriad regions come to audience.

translations.literal: Rites are rich, music abundant; solemn and august.
translations.idiomatic: Rites abound, music overflows—solemn, august, and grand.

translations.literal: : Broad flows that river; it pays homage at the Heaven Pool.
translations.idiomatic: : Wide flows the stream, turning toward the great heavenly pool.

translations.literal: Plentiful are tribute duties; measured is ritual bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute flows in abundance; dignity and bearing are composed.

translations.literal: Having mastered ritual bearing, they are also practiced in ceremonial deportment.
translations.idiomatic: Once ritual bearing is learned, ceremonial grace comes naturally.

translations.literal: When one man has the pattern, faith is stirred in every state.
translations.idiomatic: The One Man holds the measure; all realms trust in him.

translations.literal: : How abundant is our emperor, truly spirit-born, sage incarnate.
translations.idiomatic: : Abundant is our sovereign—truly spirit-sent, truly sage-born.

translations.literal: At year's beginning he takes the start; he responds to Heaven in blessed celebration.
translations.idiomatic: He stands at the year's first threshold and offers Heaven this blessed rejoicing.

translations.literal: Lofty as Heaven, splendid as the sun.
translations.idiomatic: High as heaven itself, bright as the rising sun.

translations.literal: Through this splendid blessing, the great mandate is forever secured.
translations.idiomatic: May this bright fortune endure and the great mandate stand firm forever.

sentences.zh: ::右三曲，別用金石，太樂令跪奏。

translations.literal: :: Right: three pieces—metal and stone used separately; the Grand Musician kneels to announce performance.
translations.idiomatic: :: Right: three movements—metal and stone played apart; the Director of Grand Music kneels to announce them.

translations.literal: Food-raising hymn text:
translations.idiomatic: Hymn for raising the feast:

translations.literal: : Morning rites blaze forth; all things behold.
translations.idiomatic: : Morning ceremony blazes bright; every creature looks on.

translations.literal: Good celebration spans three courts; rite and music are fully performed.
translations.idiomatic: Blessing fills three reigns; rite and music stand complete.

translations.literal: At New Year's first beginning, statutes and patterns shine clear.
translations.idiomatic: At the year's first dawn, laws and emblems shine clear.

translations.literal: Ten thousand regions come to congratulate; Chinese and barbarian fill the court.
translations.idiomatic: The myriad regions come to congratulate; Chinese and foreign envoys fill the court.

sentences.zh: 多士盈九德，俯仰觀玉聲。

translations.literal: Multitudes of scholars fill the nine virtues; bowing and rising they watch the jade tones.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars of every virtue fill the hall; bowing and rising they heed the jade chime's tone.

translations.literal: Gentle in bow and rise; their splendor spreads abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Reverent in every bow and rise, they wear a shining grace.

sentences.zh: 鍾鼓震天區，禮容塞皇闈。

translations.literal: Bells and drums shake the heavenly realm; ritual bearing fills the imperial gate.
translations.idiomatic: Bells and drums shake the heavens; ritual bearing fills the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 思樂窮休慶，福履同所歸。

translations.literal: Thought and music reach the utmost blessing; fortune's path returns to the same home.
translations.idiomatic: Joy and music exhaust all blessing; fortune and blessing share one returning path.

translations.literal: : Five jades already offered; three silks are presented.
translations.idiomatic: : The five jades have been offered; the three silks are set forth.

translations.literal: You dukes, you marquises, jade clappers sound in the splendid hall.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes and marquises alike—jade pendants ring in the splendid hall.

translations.literal: August, august is the holy sovereign; he descends in rite facing south.
translations.idiomatic: August is the sacred sovereign; he receives rites facing south.

sentences.zh: 元首納嘉禮，萬邦同欽願。

translations.literal: The chief accepts the fine tribute; all states share reverent wish.
translations.idiomatic: The head of state receives fine tribute; every realm shares one reverent wish.

translations.literal: Blessed, blessed—the lord and ministers feast in radiance.
translations.idiomatic: Blessing upon blessing—lord and ministers feast in harmony.

translations.literal: Five banners are raised; four suspended sets arrayed.
translations.idiomatic: Five banners rise; four bell-sets stand in ranks.

translations.literal: Music has pattern; rite knows no weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Music holds pattern; rite never grows weary.

translations.literal: Imperial wind is blended; one transformation is brought to completion.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial wind melts every heart; one transformation runs its course.

translations.literal: : Rite reaches harmony; yin and yang are moved.
translations.idiomatic: : Rite reaches perfect harmony and stirs yin and yang.

translations.literal: Virtue softens without exception; it binds blessed omens.
translations.idiomatic: All virtue turns gentle; blessed signs gather round.

translations.literal: Auspicious signs appear; the fine bell answers.
translations.idiomatic: Omens open the way; the auspicious bell sounds in answer.

translations.literal: Cloud phoenixes dance; hidden dragons leap.
translations.idiomatic: Cloud-phoenixes dance; dragons hidden in the deep leap up.

translations.literal: The Luminous Star appears; sweet dew falls.
translations.idiomatic: The Bright Star appears; sweet dew falls.

translations.literal: Joined-trunk trees; grain with shared ears.
translations.idiomatic: Trees grow with joined trunks; grain shares one ear.

translations.literal: Dark transformation harmonizes; benevolent grace spreads.
translations.idiomatic: The dark transformation spreads in harmony; benevolent grace is poured abroad.

translations.literal: Ultimate auspicious omens; spirit talismans to the limit.
translations.idiomatic: Peak auspicious signs appear; spirit tokens reach their end.

translations.literal: : Cherishing the distant wilds, he pacifies all the people.
translations.idiomatic: : He embraces the far wastes; he calms the people as one.

translations.literal: Bearing Heaven's blessing, none fail to submit as guests.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's blessing rests on him; none fail to come as guests.

translations.literal: None fail to submit as guests; long ages flourish.
translations.idiomatic: All come as guests; long ages know splendor.

translations.literal: Bright clarity has fusion; abundant blessed celebration.
translations.idiomatic: Bright clarity blends as one; rich blessings multiply.

translations.literal: Abundant blessed celebration; the emperor's reign shines.
translations.idiomatic: Blessings heap on blessings; the imperial reign grows bright.

translations.literal: Vital breath moves in sympathetic response; the common people joyfully uphold him.
translations.idiomatic: Breath and feeling answer one another; the people gladly uphold him.

translations.literal: The three numinous powers unite in auspicious signs; only the new imperial age.
translations.idiomatic: The three powers join in auspicious signs; the new imperial age alone.

translations.literal: : The kingly Way reaches the four quarters; benevolence and virtue flow.
translations.idiomatic: : The kingly Way reaches four ways; benevolence spreads abroad.

sentences.zh: 窮理詠乾元，垂訓從帝則。

translations.literal: He exhausts principle and chants Qian Origin; he hands down instruction following the emperor's norm.
translations.idiomatic: He probes principle and sings the primal origin; he hands down teaching after the emperor's rule.

sentences.zh: 靈化侔四時，幽誠通玄默。

translations.literal: Spirit transformation matches the four seasons; hidden sincerity penetrates the dark silence.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit-change matches the four seasons; hidden sincerity pierces the dark silence.

sentences.zh: 德澤被八紘，禮章軌萬國。

translations.literal: Virtue's grace covers the eight cords; ritual pattern guides ten thousand states.
translations.idiomatic: Virtue's grace covers the eight reaches; ritual law guides every state.

translations.literal: : Imperial designs are gathered; all rejoice in peace.
translations.idiomatic: : Royal counsel is gathered whole; all flourish in peace.

sentences.zh: 禮儀煥帝庭，要荒服遐外。

translations.literal: Rites and etiquette blaze in the imperial court; the remote borderlands submit from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Court rites blaze bright; the farthest wastes bow from afar.

sentences.zh: 被髪襲纓冕，左衽回衿帶。

translations.literal: With disheveled hair they don crown and cap; left-lapel folk turn back their robe-belts.
translations.idiomatic: Wild-haired peoples don caps and coronets; left-lapel folk turn back their girdles.

translations.literal: Heaven covers, earth bears; grace flows vast and deep.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven covers and earth bears; beneficent streams pour in breadth.

translations.literal: Sound and teaching spread broadly; virtue's light grows great.
translations.idiomatic: His transforming voice spreads wide; virtue's light grows great.
