translations.literal: : Opening the primal season, all come to court as kings.
translations.idiomatic: : The primal age opens; all come to court as kings.

translations.literal: Bearing tribute duties, they attend the empress and emperor.
translations.idiomatic: They bear tribute and attend the empress and emperor at court.

translations.literal: Jade pendants ring; they observe statutes and patterns.
translations.idiomatic: Jade pendants chime; they study statute and rite.

translations.literal: They delight in the king's celebration; pleased with splendid fragrance.
translations.idiomatic: They rejoice in the royal feast; they savor noble grace.

translations.literal: Pottery-molded flourishing transformation; they roam in great peace.
translations.idiomatic: Shaped by great transforming influence, they roam in abundant peace.

translations.literal: Only brightness; forever may it flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Only radiance shines; forever may it flourish.

translations.literal: : Only in founding the primal era, virtue greatly displayed.
translations.idiomatic: : In the founding primal reign, virtue shines supreme.

translations.literal: He aligns the seven regulators; he spreads the five canons.
translations.idiomatic: He aligns the seven regulators; he spreads the five canons.

translations.literal: Constant norms ordered; grand transformation declared.
translations.idiomatic: Eternal norms are set in order; the great transformation spreads.

translations.literal: : The king's grace flows; Great Peace begins.
translations.idiomatic: : Royal grace flows abroad; Great Peace begins.

translations.literal: Spirit shrines are established; sacrifices reverently brightened.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit shrines are raised; bright sacrifices are reverently done.

translations.literal: Bordering on bright fortune; he receives blessed felicity.
translations.idiomatic: He nears glorious fortune; he receives blessed grace.

translations.literal: Rite has bearing; music has pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Rite has its bearing; music has its forms.

translations.literal: Metal and stone are arrayed; shield-feathers are displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Bells and stones are arrayed; shield-dances are performed.

translations.literal: Surpassing "Wu" and "Huo," matching "Xian Pool."
translations.idiomatic: Surpassing "Wu" and "Huo," matching "Xian Pool."

translations.literal: They sing "Southern Breeze"; virtue is forever praised.
translations.idiomatic: They sing "Southern Breeze"; his virtue is praised forever.

translations.literal: Civil splendor blazes; eulogy voices rise.
translations.idiomatic: Culture's glory blazes; songs of praise arise.

translations.literal: : The kingly Way is pure; virtue grows ever more good.
translations.idiomatic: : The kingly Way stands pure; virtue grows ever more gentle.

translations.literal: He pacifies the eight directions; the nine domains know peace.
translations.idiomatic: He calms the eight reaches; the nine domains know peace.

translations.literal: He guides ritual yielding; he moves customs and mores.
translations.idiomatic: He guides courtesy and yielding; he shifts customs.

translations.literal: Customs and mores are moved; forever they blend as one.
translations.idiomatic: Customs shift; forever they blend as one.

translations.literal: They sing the flourishing beauty; they announce accomplished merit.
translations.idiomatic: They sing abundant glory; they proclaim success complete.

translations.literal: They chant the beautiful achievement; far, without end.
translations.idiomatic: They chant glorious deeds—far, without end.

sentences.zh: ::右黃鐘先奏《晨儀》篇，太蔟奏《五玉》篇，餘八篇二廂更奏之。

translations.literal: :: Right: Yellow Bell gallery first plays the "Morning Rite" chapter; Great Clarity plays the "Five Jades" chapter; the remaining eight chapters alternate between the two wings.
translations.idiomatic: :: Right: Yellow Bell gallery first plays "Morning Rite"; Great Clarity plays "Five Jades"; the other eight pieces alternate between the two wings.

translations.literal: "Front Dance" stair-step song lyrics: new text
translations.idiomatic: "Front Dance" stair-song lyrics: new text

translations.literal: : Heaven raises the sage and wise; the three directions are the sustaining net.
translations.idiomatic: : Heaven raises the sage and wise; the three realms hold the net of order.

translations.literal: Rivers and mountains are at peace; the seven luminaries shine again.
translations.idiomatic: Rivers and mountains rest in peace; the seven lights shine anew.

translations.literal: Luxuriantly he nurtures myriad things; the multitude all know peace.
translations.idiomatic: He richly nourishes all things; the people all know peace.

translations.literal: The Way's use secretly penetrates; benevolence spreads far.
translations.idiomatic: The Way works hidden yet through; benevolence spreads to distant lands.

translations.literal: Virtue thick as Kun Peak; merit high as vast azure Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Virtue stands thick as Kun Peak; merit towers high as bright Heaven.

translations.literal: Elephant dance in grand appearance; virtue is hymned in song.
translations.idiomatic: Elephant-dance fills the pageant; virtue is hymned in song.

translations.literal: The eight sounds already measured; dragon leaps and phoenix soars.
translations.idiomatic: All eight tones are tuned; dragon and phoenix seem to soar in flight.

translations.literal: The imperial foundation is planted forever; Heaven and Earth are equal in span.
translations.idiomatic: The throne is rooted for ages; Heaven and Earth share one span.

translations.literal: "Front Dance Triumphant Appearance" song-poem: old text
translations.idiomatic: "Front Dance Triumphant Appearance" hymn: old wording

translations.literal: : Glorious is the bright mandate; Heaven's mirror draws nigh.
translations.idiomatic: : Splendid the radiant mandate; Heaven looks down in judgment.

translations.literal: Music comes from the yang side; rite is performed on the yin side.
translations.idiomatic: Music rises from the yang quarter; ritual is shaped in the yin.

translations.literal: Song springs from abundant virtue; dance arises from deep merit.
translations.idiomatic: Song wells from full virtue; dance flows from deeds deep-rooted.

translations.literal: In the court the palace bells are arrayed; on the steps zithers and lutes are spread.
translations.idiomatic: Court bells hang in the yard; lutes and zithers deck the stair.

translations.literal: Feathered panpipes and mouth-organs richly converge; pipes and stone chimes blend in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Panpipes and flutes crowd the hall; reed pipes and stone tones chime as one.

translations.literal: "Flute Shao" is ancient, yet its nine movements are performed today.
translations.idiomatic: Though "Flute Shao" is antique, its nine playings sound here now.

translations.literal: It guides the will and harmonizes the tones; the sound of virtue is greatly proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Will is led and voices joined; virtue's music rings far and clear.

translations.literal: It brightens our imperial foundation; spirits join in matching Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: It lights our throne's foundation; gods and Heaven are matched as one.

translations.literal: It models form for the six directions; transforming grace proclaims itself.
translations.idiomatic: It shapes the six reaches; quiet transformation spreads of itself.

translations.literal: Like the River of Stars, it becomes a pattern in Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Like the Milky Way, it writes its pattern on the sky.

translations.literal: Flourishing, thriving—the myriad beings; harmony molded in this year.
translations.idiomatic: All creation teems in joy; this year is shaped in harmony.

translations.literal: Striking the hub, it hits the mark of Shao; for endless ages it is not withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Wheel-hub beats mark the Shao; age on age it never slips away.

translations.literal: "Rear Dance" step-and-stair song text: new text
translations.idiomatic: "Rear Dance" step hymn: new wording

translations.literal: : August is our sovereign; the inherited enterprise flourishes bright.
translations.idiomatic: : Majestic is our lord; the line he inherits burns bright and clear.

translations.literal: Washing and brushing away defilement; the cosmos bears clarity.
translations.idiomatic: He cleanses and sweeps away stain; the whole universe turns pure.

translations.literal: Truly holding the center and harmony; he comes before the myriad people.
translations.idiomatic: He holds true mean and harmony; he rules the living folk.

translations.literal: Mysterious transformation spreads far; a thousand ages trace his form.
translations.idiomatic: His subtle teaching spreads abroad; ten thousand years take his mold.

translations.literal: How to exalt virtue? Thus the "Nine Completions" were made.
translations.idiomatic: How to honor merit?—the "Nine Completions" were wrought.

translations.literal: Graceful steps, respectful and measured; elegant tunes, fragrant and fine.
translations.idiomatic: Fair steps move slow and grave; noble airs breathe sweet scent.

translations.literal: The eight winds clear the drums; they answer with auspicious omens.
translations.idiomatic: Eight winds clear the drums; good omens answer the call.

translations.literal: His grace fills all under Heaven; his merit matches the hundred spirits.
translations.idiomatic: His bounty floods the realm; his worth matches the hundred gods.

translations.literal: "Rear Dance Triumphant Appearance" song text: old text
translations.idiomatic: "Rear Dance Triumphant Appearance" hymn: old wording

translations.literal: : O happy the sacred sovereign—truly Heaven brought forth his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: : Bless the holy lord—Heaven itself gave birth to his power.

translations.literal: Beauty gathered from within; royal plans fill the four marches.
translations.idiomatic: Grace piled up from the heart; royal counsel fills every border.

translations.literal: The dragon flies in Heaven; he models form for the myriad states.
translations.idiomatic: The dragon soars in the sky; his pattern shapes ten thousand realms.

translations.literal: Reverent and clear—divine; at court, deep and silent.
translations.idiomatic: Reverent, luminous, and godlike—on the throne, deep and still.

translations.literal: Transformation without words; every thing attains its place.
translations.idiomatic: Teaching without words; all creatures find their due.

translations.literal: He reports completion to Heaven; merit is carved in inscription.
translations.idiomatic: He tells Heaven the work is done; his feats are cut in stone.

translations.literal: Cautious are his designs; tireless is his benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: His counsel stands firm and sure; his kindness never wearies.

translations.literal: Following the mandate he creates institutions; thereby he fixes and harmonizes the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: By Heaven's charge he makes the laws; thus spirits are set at peace.

translations.literal: Beyond the sea there is peace; the nine regions know no dust.
translations.idiomatic: Peace reaches past the seas; the nine realms are free of strife.

translations.literal: With cap-strings he holds the tally; arms draped, he oversees the people.
translations.idiomatic: Tassels mark his seal of rule; hands at rest, he governs the folk.

translations.literal: Then they dance "Triumphant Appearance," reverent as Heaven and man.
translations.idiomatic: They dance "Triumphant Appearance," in awe as of Heaven and man.

translations.literal: Pure blessing, greatly auspicious; ten thousand ages ever renew.
translations.idiomatic: Blessing pure and grand; age on age it shines anew.

translations.literal: "Proclaiming Martial Glory Dance": holding shield and battle-axe.
translations.idiomatic: The "Proclaiming Martial Glory" dance is danced with shield and axe.

sentences.zh: 郊廟奏，平冕，黑介幘，玄衣裳，白領袖、絳領袖中衣，絳合幅袴，絳襪。

translations.literal: For suburban and temple performance: plain coronet, black kerchief-cap, dark upper and lower garments, white- and crimson-collared inner robe, crimson joined-panel trousers, crimson socks.
translations.idiomatic: At suburban altar and temple: plain coronet, black side-cap, dark robe, inner garment with white and crimson collar and sleeves, crimson joined trousers and socks.

sentences.zh: 朝廷，則武冠，赤幘，生絳袍單衣，絹領袖，皂領袖中衣，虎文畫合幅袴，白布彩，皆黑韋緹。

translations.literal: At court: military cap, red kerchief, unlined crimson robe as single garment, silk-collared sleeves, black-collared inner robe, tiger-pattern painted joined-panel trousers, white cloth sash—all with black leather shoe-bindings.
translations.idiomatic: In court: martial cap and red kerchief, unlined crimson robe, silk-trimmed collar and sleeves over a black-collared inner robe, tiger-striped joined trousers and white cloth sash, all with black leather gaiters.

translations.literal: Zhou's "Great Martial Dance"—Qin changed it to "Five Phases."
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou "Great Martial" dance was renamed "Five Phases" under Qin.

sentences.zh: 漢高造《武德舞》，執干戚，象天下樂己除亂。

translations.literal: Han Gaozu created the "Martial Virtue Dance," holding shield and axe, symbolizing that all under Heaven rejoiced he had ended disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu of Han devised the "Martial Virtue" dance with shield and axe, showing the realm glad he had quelled rebellion.

sentences.zh: 按《禮》云「朱干玉戚，冕而舞《大武》」，是則漢放此舞而立也。

translations.literal: The Rites says: "With vermilion shields and jade axes, in coronet dancing 'Great Martial'"—thus Han modeled this dance in establishing it.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites reads: "Vermilion shields, jade battle-axes, coroneted to dance 'Great Martial'"—so Han founded its dance on that model.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝改《五行》還爲《大武》，而《武德》曰《武頌舞》。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei changed "Five Phases" back to "Great Martial," while "Martial Virtue" was styled "Martial Hymn Dance."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi of Wei restored "Five Phases" to "Great Martial"; "Martial Virtue" became the "Martial Hymn" dance.

translations.literal: Emperor Ming remade it as the "Martial Beginning Dance."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Wei refashioned it as the "Martial Beginning" dance.

translations.literal: In the Jin age it remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Jin kept the earlier arrangement.

sentences.zh: 傅玄六代舞歌有《武》辭，此《武舞》非一也。

translations.literal: Fu Xuan's six-dynasties dance songs have a "Martial" text; these "martial dances" are not a single thing.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan's six-ages dance lyrics include a "Martial" piece—these martial dances are not all one dance.

sentences.zh: 宋孝建初，朝議以《凱容舞》爲《韶舞》，《宣烈舞》爲《武舞》。

translations.literal: In early Xiaojian of Song, court discussion made "Triumphant Appearance Dance" the "Shao Dance" and "Proclaiming Martial Glory Dance" the "Martial Dance."
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Song Xiaojian, the court ruled that "Triumphant Appearance" would stand for "Shao" and "Proclaiming Martial Glory" for the martial dance.

sentences.zh: 據《韶》爲言，《宣烈》卽是古之《大武》，非《武德》也。

translations.literal: Taking "Shao" as the point, "Proclaiming Martial Glory" is the ancient "Great Martial"—not "Martial Virtue."
translations.idiomatic: By the logic of "Shao," "Proclaiming Martial Glory" is the old "Great Martial," not the "Martial Virtue" dance.

translations.literal: In this age the popular saying calls it "King Wu's attack on Zhou."
translations.idiomatic: Today people colloquially call it "King Wu smites Zhou."

sentences.zh: 其冠服，魏明帝世尚書所奏定《武始舞》服，晉、宋承用，齊初仍舊，不改宋舞名。

translations.literal: Its caps and robes: in Emperor Ming of Wei's time the Secretariat memorial fixed the attire for "Martial Beginning Dance"; Jin and Song continued their use; at the beginning of Qi the old practice remained, without changing the Song dance names.
translations.idiomatic: Its caps and robes: under Wei Emperor Ming the Secretariat fixed the "Martial Beginning Dance" costume; Jin and Song kept it; at Qi's founding the old use stood, and the Song dance names were left unchanged.

sentences.zh: 其舞人冠服，見魏尚書奏，後代相承用之。

translations.literal: The dancers' caps and robes are given in the Wei Secretariat memorial; later generations continued to use them in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The dancers' dress is set out in the Wei Secretariat memorial; later ages handed it down unchanged.

translations.literal: "Triumphant Appearance Dance" — holding feathers and yue flutes.
translations.idiomatic: "Triumphant Appearance Dance"—with feathers and flutes in hand.

translations.literal: At suburban altars and temples: weimao cap; dress as before.
translations.idiomatic: At suburban altars and temples: weimao cap; the rest of the dress as before.

sentences.zh: 朝廷，進賢冠，黑介幘，生黃袍單衣，白合幅袴，餘如前。

translations.literal: At court: scholar-advancement crown, black jieze headband, unprocessed yellow robe jacket, white joined-panel trousers — the rest as before.
translations.idiomatic: At court: scholar-advancement crown, black jieze, unbleached yellow robe jacket, white joined-panel trousers—the rest as before.

sentences.zh: 本舜《韶舞》，漢高改曰《文始》，魏復曰《大韶》。

translations.literal: Originally Shun's "Shao Dance"; Han Gaozu changed it to "Civil Beginning"; Wei restored the name "Great Shao."
translations.idiomatic: It began as Shun's "Shao Dance"; Han Gaozu renamed it "Civil Beginning"; Wei brought back "Great Shao."

translations.literal: Also created "All-Prospering" as the "civil dance."
translations.idiomatic: Wei also fashioned "All-Prospering" as the civil dance.

sentences.zh: 晉傅玄六代舞有《虞韶舞》辭。

translations.literal: In Jin, Fu Xuan's six-dynasty dances include lyrics for "Yu Shao Dance."
translations.idiomatic: Jin Fu Xuan's six-dynasty dance set has lyrics for the "Yu Shao Dance."

translations.literal: Song made "Triumphant Appearance" succeed "Shao" as the "civil dance."
translations.idiomatic: Song made "Triumphant Appearance" follow "Shao" as the civil dance.

translations.literal: In succession they used Wei All-Prospering caps and robes.
translations.idiomatic: In succession they wore the Wei All-Prospering costume.

translations.literal: "Front Dance" and "Rear Dance" — Jin creations.
translations.idiomatic: "Front Dance" and "Rear Dance"—creations of Jin.

sentences.zh: 《正德大豫舞》，傅玄、張華各爲歌辭。

translations.literal: "Correct Virtue" and "Great Abundance Dance" — Fu Xuan and Zhang Hua each wrote song lyrics.
translations.idiomatic: "Correct Virtue" and "Great Abundance Dance"—Fu Xuan and Zhang Hua each supplied song words.

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉中，改《正德》爲《前舞》，《大豫》爲《後舞》。

translations.literal: In Song's Yuanjia era, "Correct Virtue" was changed to "Front Dance," "Great Abundance" to "Rear Dance."
translations.idiomatic: In Song's Yuanjia reign, "Correct Virtue" became "Front Dance" and "Great Abundance" became "Rear Dance."

translations.literal: :: Right: court assembly music lyrics.
translations.idiomatic: :: Right: court assembly music lyrics.

translations.literal: [=] Section divider in the source text.
translations.idiomatic: [=] Section divider in the source text.

translations.literal: Dance pieces
translations.idiomatic: Dance pieces

sentences.zh: =舞曲，皆古辭雅音，稱述功德，宴享所奏。

translations.literal: = Dance pieces: all ancient lyrics in elegant sounds, praising merit and virtue, performed at feasts and banquets.
translations.idiomatic: = Dance pieces: ancient lyrics in elegant tones, praising merit and virtue, played at feasts and banquets.

sentences.zh: 傅玄歌辭云：「獲罪於天，北徙朔方，墳墓誰掃，超若流光。

translations.literal: Fu Xuan's song lyrics say: 「Having offended Heaven, northward I migrate to the northern wastes; who will sweep my graves—swift as flowing light.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan's lyric runs: 「I have sinned against Heaven and am banished north to the frontier; who will tend my graves—gone swift as streaming light.

sentences.zh: 」如此十餘小曲，名爲舞曲，疑非宴樂之辭。

translations.literal: 」 Thus more than ten such small pieces, called dance pieces — suspected not to be feast-music lyrics.
translations.idiomatic: 」 More than ten such short pieces were called dance pieces—likely not words for banquet music.

translations.literal: Yet the general name "dance pieces" arose from this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the general name "dance pieces" took its start here.

translations.literal: "Illustrious Lord" lyrics:
translations.idiomatic: "Illustrious Lord" lyrics:

translations.literal: : The illustrious lord founded great enterprise; abundant virtue was established at the founding era.
translations.idiomatic: : The illustrious lord raised a great enterprise; his ample virtue was fixed at the founding age.

sentences.zh: 受命君四海，聖皇應靈乾。

translations.literal: Receiving the mandate he rules the four seas; the sage emperor responds to numinous Qian.
translations.idiomatic: He took the mandate and rules the four seas; the sage emperor answers Heaven's sign.

sentences.zh: 五帝繼三皇，三皇世所歸。

translations.literal: The Five Emperors succeeded the Three August Ones; the Three August Ones were the age's goal.
translations.idiomatic: Five Emperors followed Three August Ones; on the Three August Ones the age converged.

sentences.zh: 聖德應期運，天地不能違。

translations.literal: Sage virtue responds to the age's fortune; Heaven and Earth cannot oppose.
translations.idiomatic: Sage virtue meets the turning of the age; Heaven and Earth cannot stand against it.

sentences.zh: 仰之彌已高，猶天不可階。

translations.literal: Looking up, it grows ever higher; still like Heaven—not to be climbed.
translations.idiomatic: The higher one looks, the loftier it stands—like Heaven, with no stair to climb.

sentences.zh: 將復結繩化，靜拱天下齊。

translations.literal: He shall again return to the age of knotted cords; quietly folding his hands, all under Heaven is equal.
translations.idiomatic: He will restore the age of knotted cords; hands folded in stillness, all under Heaven made one.

translations.literal: :: Right: one piece — made by Han Emperor Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: :: Right: one movement—composed by Han Emperor Zhang.

translations.literal: The "Fife Dance Song" says 「In the east pass there is a worthy woman.」
translations.idiomatic: The "Fife Dance Song" has 「East of the pass lives a worthy woman.」

sentences.zh: 魏明帝代漢曲云，「明明魏皇帝」。

translations.literal: Wei Emperor Ming replaced the Han piece, saying 「Bright, bright Emperor of Wei.」
translations.idiomatic: Wei Emperor Ming replaced the Han lyric with 「Bright, bright Emperor of Wei.」

sentences.zh: 傅玄代魏曲作晉《洪業篇》云：「宣文創洪業，盛德存泰始。

translations.literal: Fu Xuan, replacing the Wei piece, made Jin's "Great Enterprise" piece, saying: 「Xuanwen founded great enterprise; abundant virtue endures from Taishi's founding.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan, replacing the Wei lyric, wrote Jin's "Great Enterprise" piece: 「Xuanwen raised the great enterprise; ample virtue holds from Taishi's founding.

sentences.zh: 聖皇應靈符，受命君四海。

translations.literal: The sage emperor responds to the numinous tally; receiving the mandate he rules the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: The sage emperor answers the numinous sign; taking the mandate he rules the four seas.

sentences.zh: 」今前四句錯綜其辭，從「五帝」至「不可階」六句全玄辭，後二句本云「將復御龍氏，鳳皇在庭栖」，又改易焉。

translations.literal: 」 Now the first four lines weave their wording; from 「Five Emperors」 through 「cannot climb」 the six lines are entirely Xuan's lyrics; the last two lines originally said 「shall again mount the Dragon-Lord's carriage, phoenixes dwelling in the court,」 and were altered again.
translations.idiomatic: 」 Today the first four lines mix their phrasing; from 「Five Emperors」 through 「no stair to climb」 all six lines are Fu Xuan's; the last two once read 「shall again ride the Dragon Lord's carriage, phoenixes roosting in the court,」 and were changed once more.

translations.literal: "Sagely Lord" lyrics:
translations.idiomatic: "Sagely Lord" lyrics:

translations.literal: : The sagely lord receives Heaven's mandate; responding to the age is Yu and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: : The sagely lord takes Heaven's mandate; in his season he is Yu and Tang.

sentences.zh: 升旒綜萬機，端扆馭八方。

translations.literal: Ascending the tassels he threads all affairs; upright at the screen he drives the eight directions.
translations.idiomatic: He mounts the tasseled cap and gathers every thread of rule; seated at the screen he steers the eight directions.

sentences.zh: 盈虛自然數，揖讓歸聖明。

translations.literal: Full and empty follow nature's numbers; yielding returns to sage brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: Plenty and want obey nature's count; by yielding, all returns to sage light.

sentences.zh: 北化陵河塞，南威越滄溟。

translations.literal: North transforms the Ling and river passes; south authority crosses the blue sea.
translations.idiomatic: North his teaching reaches the Ling and the frontier passes; south his might crosses the blue sea.

sentences.zh: 廣德齊七政，敷教騰三辰。

translations.literal: Broad virtue aligns the seven regulators; spreading teaching rises with the three luminaries.
translations.idiomatic: Broad virtue matches the seven regulators; his teaching soars with sun, moon, and stars.

sentences.zh: 萬㝢必承慶，百福咸來臻。

translations.literal: All realms surely receive blessed celebration; hundred fortunes all arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Every quarter must share his blessing; a hundred fortunes gather at his throne.

sentences.zh: 聖皇應福始，昌德洞祐先。

translations.literal: The sage emperor responds to fortune's source; flourishing virtue penetrates blessing before.
translations.idiomatic: The sage emperor answers where fortune begins; thriving virtue opens blessing beforehand.

translations.literal: "Illustrious Lord" lyrics:
translations.idiomatic: "Illustrious Lord" lyrics:

translations.literal: : The illustrious lord rules the four seas; his overall mirror exhausts all human spirits.
translations.idiomatic: : The illustrious lord holds the four seas; his full mirror takes in every soul.

sentences.zh: 仰成恩已洽，竭忠身必榮。

translations.literal: Looking up, his accomplished grace is already complete; exhausting loyalty, the person must be honored.
translations.idiomatic: Look up—his grace already runs full; pour out loyalty and honor is sure.

sentences.zh: 聖澤洞三靈，德教被八鄉。

translations.literal: Sage bounty penetrates the three numina; virtue's teaching covers the eight hamlets.
translations.idiomatic: Sacred favor pierces the three spirits; his teaching clothes the eight directions.

sentences.zh: 草木變柯葉，川岳洞嘉祥。

translations.literal: Grass and trees change their branches and leaves; rivers and mountains reveal auspicious signs.
translations.idiomatic: Grass and trees shift branch and leaf; rivers and hills shine with good omens.

sentences.zh: 愉樂盛明運，舞蹈升太時。

translations.literal: Joyful music in the flourishing bright age; dancing rises to the grandest season.
translations.idiomatic: Delight in the bright flourishing age; dance lifts to the grandest hour.

sentences.zh: 微霜永昌命，軌心長歡怡。

translations.literal: Light frost, ever-abundant mandate; steadfast heart, long joy and ease.
translations.idiomatic: Light frost, mandate ever full; loyal heart, lasting joy and peace.

translations.literal: "Bell-clapper Dance" song lyrics:
translations.idiomatic: "Bell-clapper Dance" song lyrics:

sentences.zh: :黃《雲門》，唐《咸池》，虞《韶舞》，夏《夏》殷《濩》，列代有五。

translations.literal: : Yellow Thearch's "Cloud Gate," Tang's "Salty Pool," Yu's "Shao Dance," Xia's "Xia," Shang's "Hu" — five successive eras.
translations.idiomatic: : Yellow Thearch's "Cloud Gate," Tang's "Salty Pool," Yu's "Shao," Xia's "Xia," Shang's "Hu"—five dynasties in a row.

translations.literal: Shake the bell-clapper, sound the metal bells; extend "Great Martial."
translations.idiomatic: Bell and bronze ring out; "Great Martial" carries on.

translations.literal: Clear song begins to sing; form is master.
translations.idiomatic: Clear song lifts its voice; the body's form is lord.

translations.literal: Sound harmonizes with the eight tones; it accords with pitch-pipes and pitch-standards.
translations.idiomatic: Voices blend with the eight timbres; pitch-pipes and standards fall in tune.

translations.literal: The body does not move in vain; the hands do not rise without purpose.
translations.idiomatic: No idle motion of the body; no empty lift of the hands.

translations.literal: Responding to measure, matching degree, cycling through order.
translations.idiomatic: Each beat meets its measure; the dance wheels through its ordered rounds.

translations.literal: At times they play gong and jue, mingled with zhi and yu.
translations.idiomatic: Now gong and jue are sounded, now zhi and yu are woven in.

sentences.zh: 樂以移風，禮相輔，安有出其所。

translations.literal: Music shifts the wind of custom; rite assists it—how could there be departure from its place?
translations.idiomatic: Music shifts custom; rite shores it up—how could either step outside its role?

sentences.zh: ::右一曲，傅玄辭，以代魏《太和時》。

translations.literal: :: Right: one piece—text by Fu Xuan, replacing Wei "Tahe Times."
translations.idiomatic: :: Right: one movement—lyrics by Fu Xuan, in place of the Wei piece "Tahe Times."

sentences.zh: 「徵羽」下除「下厭衆目，上從鐘鼓」二句。

translations.literal: Below "zhi and yu" two lines were removed: "below to glut the crowd's eyes; above to follow bells and drums."
translations.idiomatic: Under the "zhi and yu" passage two lines were cut: "below to glut every eye; above to trail bell and drum."

translations.literal: "White Dove" hymn text:
translations.idiomatic: "White Dove" hymn text:

translations.literal: : Fluttering white dove, flying again, crying again.
translations.idiomatic: : Light white dove, soaring once more, calling once more.

translations.literal: Cherishing our lord's virtue, it comes to gather in the lord's court.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of our lord's grace, it alights in the lord's hall.

sentences.zh: ::右一曲，《舞敘》云：「《白符》或云《白符鳩舞》，出江南，吳人所造。

translations.literal: :: Right: one piece—"Dance Narrative" says: "White Talisman," also called "White Talisman Dove Dance," came from south of the Yangtze; Wu men composed it.
translations.idiomatic: :: Right: one movement—"Dance Narrative" says: "White Talisman," or "White Talisman Dove Dance," arose in Jiangnan and was made by men of Wu.

sentences.zh: 其辭意言患孫皓虐政，慕政化也。

translations.literal: The meaning of the text laments Sun Hao's cruel rule and yearns for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: The lyric means to grieve Sun Hao's harsh rule and long for true reform.

sentences.zh: 其詩本云『平平白符，思我君惠，集我金堂』。

translations.literal: The poem originally read, "Even, even white talisman; I think on my lord's grace and gather in my golden hall."
translations.idiomatic: The poem originally ran, "Steady, steady white talisman; I recall my lord's bounty and gather in the golden hall."

sentences.zh: 言白者金行，符，合也，鳩亦合也。

translations.literal: "White" means the Metal phase; fu means "join," and the dove also means "join."
translations.idiomatic: "White" stands for the Metal phase; fu means union, and the dove too means union.

translations.literal: Though talisman and dove differ in word, the meaning is the same."
translations.idiomatic: Talisman and dove differ in name, but the sense is one."

translations.literal: "Ji Ji" hymn text:
translations.idiomatic: "Ji Ji" hymn text:

translations.literal: : Soaring flight, soaring dance; spirit flows fragrant.
translations.idiomatic: : Free in flight, free in dance; breath streams sweet and bright.

translations.literal: Recalling the Three and Five, great splendor of Yellow.
translations.idiomatic: They recall the Three Sovereigns and Five Thearchs, the great glory of Yellow.

sentences.zh: ::右一曲，晉《濟濟舞歌》，六解，此是最後一解。

translations.literal: :: Right: one piece—Jin "Ji Ji Dance Song," six stanzas; this is the last stanza.
translations.idiomatic: :: Right: one movement—Jin "Ji Ji Dance Song," six stanzas; this is the final stanza.

translations.literal: "Du Lu" hymn text:
translations.idiomatic: "Solitary Deer" hymn text:

translations.literal: : Du lu, du lu—waters deep, mud turbid.
translations.idiomatic: : Solitary deer, solitary deer—deep the water, foul the mud.
